newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian dep min sees changes for oil law year-end.
newsitem.headline: Russian dep min sees changes for oil law year-end.

text.p: The Fuel and Energy Ministry hopes amendments needed to reconcile tax and customs legislation with Russia's oil production-sharing law will be adopted by the end of the year, a deputy minister said on Tuesday.

"I think that by the end of the year the State Duma (lower house of parliament) will adopt amendments to tax and customs legislation and that the laws will fully correspond with the production-sharing law," Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Valery Garipov told Reuters.
He said his ministry and those of justice and natural resources had sent the necessary amendments to parliament and that hearings would be held in mid-November.
Garipov said the changes were aimed at excluding value-added tax and lifting customs duties on imported equipment and amendments to the law on natural resources.

The law on production-sharing has been passed but foreign investors say it is inadequate. Russia has promised to amend the law, taking into account comments by Western investors, especially on international arbitration issues.
